name: xmpp
title: XMPP
description: Send and receive messages to/from an XMPP chat server.
label: chat,messaging

properties.name: host
properties.description: Hostname for the chat server

properties.name: port
properties.description: Port number for the chat server

properties.name: participant
properties.label: common
properties.description: JID (Jabber ID) of person to receive messages. room parameter has precedence over participant.

properties.name: login
properties.label: common
properties.description: Whether to login the user.

properties.name: nickname
properties.label: common
properties.description: Use nickname when joining room. If room is specified and nickname is not, user will be used for the nickname.

properties.name: pubsub
properties.label: common
properties.description: Accept pubsub packets on input, default is false

properties.name: room
properties.label: common
properties.description: If this option is specified, the component will connect to MUC (Multi User Chat). Usually, the domain name for MUC is different from the login domain. For example, if you are supermanjabber.org and want to join the krypton room, then the room URL is kryptonconference.jabber.org. Note the conference part. It is not a requirement to provide the full room JID. If the room parameter does not contain the symbol, the domain part will be discovered and added by Camel

properties.name: serviceName
properties.label: common
properties.description: The name of the service you are connecting to. For Google Talk, this would be gmail.com.

properties.name: testConnectionOnStartup
properties.label: common
properties.description: Specifies whether to test the connection on startup. This is used to ensure that the XMPP client has a valid connection to the XMPP server when the route starts. Camel throws an exception on startup if a connection cannot be established. When this option is set to false, Camel will attempt to establish a lazy connection when needed by a producer, and will poll for a consumer connection until the connection is established. Default is true.

properties.name: createAccount
properties.label: common,advanced
properties.description: If true, an attempt to create an account will be made. Default is false.

properties.name: resource
properties.label: common,advanced
properties.description: XMPP resource. The default is Camel.

properties.name: connectionPollDelay
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: The amount of time in seconds between polls (in seconds) to verify the health of the XMPP connection, or between attempts to establish an initial consumer connection. Camel will try to re-establish a connection if it has become inactive. Default is 10 seconds.

properties.name: doc
properties.label: consumer
properties.description: Set a doc header on the IN message containing a Document form of the incoming packet; default is true if presence or pubsub are true, otherwise false

properties.name: bridgeErrorHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exceptionHandler
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

properties.name: exchangePattern
properties.label: consumer,advanced
properties.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

properties.name: lazyStartProducer
properties.label: producer,advanced
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: connectionConfig
properties.label: advanced
properties.description: To use an existing connection configuration. Currently org.jivesoftware.smack.tcp.XMPPTCPConnectionConfiguration is only supported (XMPP over TCP).

properties.name: headerFilterStrategy
properties.label: filter
properties.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter header to and from Camel message.

properties.name: password
properties.label: security
properties.description: Password for login

properties.name: roomPassword
properties.label: security
properties.description: Password for room

properties.name: user
properties.label: security
properties.description: User name (without server name). If not specified, anonymous login will be attempted.
